title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
slides: Disney teams with Adobe on AI—what could go wrong?
The partnership aims to streamline content creation workflows.
But animators fear AI could replace their jobs.
Studios using these tools may cut production costs, but
Will creative control shift from artists to algorithms?
thread_text:
1. Disney+Adobe: AI or Bust?

Disney just partnered with Adobe to integrate AI into its animation pipeline, aiming to speed up content creation. But animators are already worried about what this means for their jobs.

2. Faster Workflows, Fewer Jobs?

The partnership promises streamlined workflows, but critics fear it's a backdoor to replacing human animators with algorithms. Studios could cut costs by automating tasks once done by skilled artists.

3. Creative Control at Risk

As AI takes over more production tasks, the big question is: who controls the creative direction? Artists worry their unique style and vision will be overridden by algorithmic efficiency.

4. Cost Cuts vs. Quality

Studios may save money, but will the push for cheaper production sacrifice the artistry that makes Disney magic? Animators argue that AI can't replicate human creativity and emotional storytelling.

5. Your Take: AI in Animation?

Would you support AI tools in animation if they speed up production, or do you think they risk killing the craft? Share your thoughts—this affects every creative industry.

instagram.caption:
Disney animators just watched their studio partner with Adobe on generative AI for the animation pipeline.

The two companies are building tools meant to speed up content creation workflows.

Animators fear those streamlined workflows could automate tasks once done by skilled artists, not just assist them.

Studios using these tools may cut production costs, but the trade-off could be creative control shifting from artists to algorithms.

If you work in animation or content creation, the tools you're asked to use next year may be built to replace parts of your process, not support it.

Would you accept an AI tool that speeds up your work if it also learns to do your job? 🎨🤖⚠️💬
